messages.subject: lm function in geom_smooth
parts:
Hi all,


I noticed something but stop me if I'm absolutely wrong. I want to
show my data in 3 facets as points and including a regression line for
each facet using geom_smooth(method="lm").

Trying to display the equations of linerar regression on each facet, I
noticed something strange. It seems that the linear regression does
not correspond to the equation I get for fitting a lm.

Anything wrong with the lm function in geom_smooth0 ? Or is my
approach to define my equations that are completely out of line?

Here is an example with random values (and I noticed the same
problem... and sorry about this terrible coding... I'm quite new in R
and I'm starting to understand it but I'm still a beginner)

dt<-
data.frame(x=rnorm(1:120),y=rnorm(1:120),d=rep(c("a","b","c"),each=40))


g<- ggplot(dt, aes(x,y))+geom_point(size=3)+facet_grid(.~d)

g1<- g+ geom_smooth(method="lm", se=F) # the lines look more or less
fine...


#here is how I coded my equations individually, there's for sure a
more esthetic way but so far that's all I found out.

dta<-subset(dt,dt$d=="a")

m_eqn1 = function(dta){
m = lm(y ~ x, dta);
eq <- substitute(italic(y) == a + b %.%
italic(x)*","~~italic(r)^2~"="~r2,
list(a = format(coef(m)[1], digits = 2),
b = format(coef(m)[2], digits = 2),
r2 = format(summary(m)$r.squared, digits = 3)))
as.character(as.expression(eq));
}


dtb<-subset(dt,dt$d=="b")


m_eqn2 = function(dtb){
m = lm(y ~ x, dtb);
eq <- substitute(italic(y) == a + b %.%
italic(x)*","~~italic(r)^2~"="~r2,
list(a = format(coef(m)[1], digits = 2),
b = format(coef(m)[2], digits = 2),
r2 = format(summary(m)$r.squared, digits = 3)))
as.character(as.expression(eq));
}

dtc<-subset(dt,dt$d=="c")


m_eqn3 = function(dtc){
m = lm(y ~ x, dtc);
eq <- substitute(italic(y) == a + b %.%
italic(x)*","~~italic(r)^2~"="~r2,
list(a = format(coef(m)[1], digits = 2),
b = format(coef(m)[2], digits = 2),
r2 = format(summary(m)$r.squared, digits = 3)))
as.character(as.expression(eq));
}

test<- data.frame(d=c("a","b","c"),
lab=c(m_eqn1(dta),m_eqn2(dtb),m_eqn3(dtc)))

#then I included the equation in each facet, that perfectly worked

g2<-g1+ geom_text(aes(x= 0,y= 3, label=lab),data=test, parse=T)

Considering this, I thought of including my regression lines
"manually" with stat_function() but it seems to more complicated since
I couldn't create a data frame where to include each function that
describe my regression lines.

Any suggestions to solve my problems?

I already thank you!

Thomas

messages.subject: Re: lm function in geom_smooth
parts:
Hi Thomas,

I'd use ddply, as below. When I do it, the equations look ok to me.

dt <- data.frame(
x = rnorm(1:120),
y = rnorm(1:120),
d = rep(c("a","b","c"), each = 40))

ggplot(dt, aes(x, y)) +
geom_point(size = 3) +
geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = F) +
facet_grid(. ~ d)

reg_eqn <- function(df) {
m <- lm(y ~ x, data = df)

a <- coef(m)[1]
b <- coef(m)[2]
r2 <- summary(m)$r.squared

expr <- substitute(italic(y) == a + b %.% italic(x)*","~~italic(r)^2~"="~r2,
list(a = format(a, digits = 2),
b = format(b, digits = 2),
r2 = format(r2, digits = 3)))
c(lab = as.character(as.expression(expr)))
}

eqns <- ddply(dt, "d", reg_eqn)

ggplot(dt, aes(x, y)) +
geom_point(size = 3) +
geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = F) +
geom_text(aes(x = 0, y = 3, label = lab), data = eqns, parse = T) +
facet_grid(. ~ d)


Hadley
